title: Motorola Is Offering a Free Smartwatch and Earbuds When You Buy a Razr
gist: Wired promotes a Motorola deal that bundles a free Moto Watch and Swarovski Edition Moto Buds 2 Plus (valued at $350) with the $800 2026 Razr, with no discount on the phone itself.

insights.claim: Motorola is bundling a Moto Watch and Swarovski Edition Moto Buds 2 Plus earbuds, valued at $350, with the $800 2026 Razr instead of discounting the phone's MSRP.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Hardware makers are using bundles and trade-ins, not price cuts, to protect headline pricing on foldables.

insights.claim: Trade-in values cited include up to $250 or more for an iPhone, $35 for a Pixel 6 in good condition, and up to $290 for a Pixel 10.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Trade-in credits are a conquest tool aimed at Apple and Google users.

insights.claim: Wired says foldable phones are gaining popularity but high prices keep most people from buying them, and rates the $800 2026 Razr as the best budget foldable.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Sub-$1,000 foldables are the volume entry point; premium rivals include Samsung Galaxy Fold8 and Apple iPhone Duo.
insights.quote: Foldable phones are gaining popularity, but their high prices keep most people from buying them.

insights.claim: The Razr shares the Ultra's titanium-reinforced hinge and IP48 rating, uses a MediaTek chip, but promises only three Android updates and has so-so Motorola AI features.
insights.speaker: Les Shu
insights.so_what: Short software support and weak AI are the trade-offs at the budget tier.
